title: Mobile forms with the right keyboard and autofill
when: A form is painful on a phone: wrong keyboard, no autofill, the page zooms on focus, or the keyboard covers the submit button.
prompt:
Goal: A form where each field opens the right on screen keyboard, autofill fills what it can and the active field stays visible above the keyboard.
Steps:
1. Pick type and inputmode per field: type="email"; type="tel" for phones; inputmode="numeric" with pattern="[0-9]*" for codes; inputmode="decimal" for amounts; type="search" for search boxes.
2. Set autocomplete tokens: name, email, tel, street-address, postal-code, current-password, new-password, one-time-code.
3. Set enterkeyhint ("next", "done", "search", "send") so the return key says what happens.
4. Font size at least 16px on inputs so the phone does not zoom on focus; never block zoom in the viewport meta.
5. Each input has a visible <label for>; errors sit under the field, linked with aria-describedby.
6. One column layout, full width fields, submit button at least 48 px tall.
7. On focus call el.scrollIntoView({ block: "center" }) after a short delay when the visualViewport height shrinks.
8. Use autocapitalize="off" and spellcheck="false" for emails and usernames.
Quality bar:
- The form can be completed with autofill plus two taps.
- No field asks for data the task does not need.
Pitfalls:
- type="number" for card or zip codes, which drops leading zeros and shows spinners.
- Placeholders used as labels.
- Validation that fires on every key press.
Verify:
- [ ] Every input has a label and an autocomplete token.
- [ ] Inputs use 16px or larger text.
- [ ] The form submits with the return key.
Output: the form markup in index.html, form.css and form.js.

examples.input: meu formulário de cadastro no celular abre o teclado errado e dá zoom
examples.output: Fields with inputmode, autocomplete tokens, enterkeyhint, 16px inputs and aria-describedby errors
